labs.title: Load and query a Microsoft Fabric warehouse
labs.summary: Create a Fabric warehouse, load a small sales star schema with a Copy data flow, answer business questions with T-SQL, and save a reusable view.
labs.scenario: Fabrikam's sales team wants a curated relational model for recurring business questions. In the **simulated Microsoft Fabric portal** on your lab VM, create a warehouse named **SalesWarehouse** in the **Sales Analytics** workspace, load sample sales data with a **Copy data** activity, query a small star schema with T-SQL joins and aggregates, save a view named **vwRegionalSales**, and verify when a warehouse is a better fit than a lakehouse.
learningObjectives: Create a Warehouse item in a Fabric workspace
Use a Copy data activity to load a warehouse star schema
Run T-SQL joins and aggregates over fact and dimension tables
Explain warehouse versus lakehouse choices for DP-900 analytics scenarios
prerequisites: Know that a star schema has fact tables and dimension tables

steps.title: Open the Sales Analytics workspace
steps.hint: Workspaces contain Fabric items such as warehouses, lakehouses, semantic models, reports, and pipelines.
steps.explanation: Fabric items are organized in workspaces so teams can manage related data, permissions, and reports together.

steps.title: Create SalesWarehouse
steps.instruction: Select **+ New item**, choose **Warehouse**, and create **SalesWarehouse**.
steps.hint: Do not choose Lakehouse for this task; the scenario asks for a relational warehouse experience.
steps.explanation: A Fabric Warehouse is designed for relational tables, T-SQL querying, views, and downstream semantic models.

steps.title: Load the retail sales star schema
steps.instruction: Select **Get data**. In **Copy data**, use **Copy data activity**, **Sample data**, **Retail sales star schema**, destination **SalesWarehouse**, turn on **Save + run**, and select **Run**.
steps.hint: A star schema includes a fact table for measures and dimension tables for descriptive attributes.
steps.explanation: Copy data is a code-free ingestion option. Warehouses can also ingest with T-SQL, but this step shows the current guided loading experience.

steps.title: Answer total sales by region
steps.instruction: In **New SQL query**, run `SELECT fs.Region, SUM(fs.SalesAmount) AS TotalSales FROM FactSales fs GROUP BY fs.Region ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;`.
steps.hint: This query needs only the fact table because Region is stored with each sale in this sample.
steps.explanation: GROUP BY turns transaction rows into business-level totals such as sales by region.

rule.pattern: SELECT fs\.Region, SUM\(fs\.SalesAmount\) AS TotalSales FROM FactSales fs GROUP BY fs\.Region ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;?

rules.failureFeedback: Run the regional sales query exactly as shown.

steps.title: Join dimensions to answer category sales
steps.instruction: Run `SELECT p.Category, SUM(fs.SalesAmount) AS TotalSales FROM FactSales fs JOIN DimProduct p ON fs.ProductKey = p.ProductKey GROUP BY p.Category ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;`.
steps.hint: FactSales has ProductKey; DimProduct has the readable Category.
steps.explanation: Warehouse schemas commonly join a fact table to dimensions so reports can slice measures by descriptive attributes.

rules.description: Category JOIN aggregate query was run

rule.pattern: JOIN DimProduct p ON fs\.ProductKey = p\.ProductKey GROUP BY p\.Category

rules.failureFeedback: Run the sales by category query.

steps.title: Filter a business segment
steps.instruction: Run `SELECT fs.Region, c.Segment, SUM(fs.SalesAmount) AS TotalSales FROM FactSales fs JOIN DimCustomer c ON fs.CustomerKey = c.CustomerKey WHERE c.Segment = 'Wholesale' GROUP BY fs.Region, c.Segment ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;`.
steps.hint: The customer dimension stores Segment. WHERE filters rows before grouping.
steps.explanation: Analysts often filter dimension attributes, then group facts to answer narrower business questions.

rule.pattern: WHERE c\.Segment = 'Wholesale' GROUP BY fs\.Region, c\.Segment

steps.title: Save a reusable view
steps.instruction: In **Save as view**, save **vwRegionalSales** with definition **Regional sales by product category**, then open **Views** to verify it appears.
steps.hint: Views package reusable SQL logic so report builders do not rewrite the same joins and aggregates.
steps.explanation: A warehouse view is a relational object that exposes a saved query shape for downstream analytics and semantic models.

rules.failureFeedback: Save vwRegionalSales and show it in Views.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Workspaces** and open **Sales Analytics**.
2. Select **+ New item**. Choose **Warehouse** and create `SalesWarehouse`.
3. Select **Get data**. In **Copy data**, choose **Copy data activity**, **Sample data**, **Retail sales star schema**, destination **SalesWarehouse**, turn on **Save + run**, and select **Run**.
4. In **New SQL query**, run `SELECT fs.Region, SUM(fs.SalesAmount) AS TotalSales FROM FactSales fs GROUP BY fs.Region ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;`.
5. Run `SELECT p.Category, SUM(fs.SalesAmount) AS TotalSales FROM FactSales fs JOIN DimProduct p ON fs.ProductKey = p.ProductKey GROUP BY p.Category ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;`.
6. Run `SELECT fs.Region, c.Segment, SUM(fs.SalesAmount) AS TotalSales FROM FactSales fs JOIN DimCustomer c ON fs.CustomerKey = c.CustomerKey WHERE c.Segment = 'Wholesale' GROUP BY fs.Region, c.Segment ORDER BY TotalSales DESC;`.
7. In **Save as view**, save `vwRegionalSales` with **Regional sales by product category**, then open **Views** to verify it.
